brand.name: sonarly
brand.tagline: Your music. Your disk. Any client.
brand.sector: self-hosted music streaming and collection management

sentence.en: Sonarly indexes the music folder you already have and serves it through the OpenSubsonic API, so any Subsonic client works — and your files stay on your disk, in your folder structure, exactly where you left them.

set.name: Copper Echo
set.mechanism: The sonar ping that returns your own signal: one thin ring sweeps out and a single copper dot comes back — an index that answers with your collection. A warm dark room for listening, paired with a restrained warm off-white light surface so the product stays software.
set.expression_move: The copper echo dot is the only saturated moment; everything else is near-black, bone or paper.
set.differs_by: Every competitor pairs a neutral sans with a corporate primary (Navidrome blue, Jellyfin cyan, Plex magenta, Ampache orange); this is the only warm dark room with a single deep-copper signal, now with a light surface that belongs to the same environment.

logo.concept: A sonar sweep and its echo, nothing more: an open ring and one copper dot. The mark is kept to two primitives so it survives every size and becomes the interface's signal language.

defaults_used.why: Echo Copper is the echo dot of the brand's namesake mechanism (Sonarly = sonar), not a clay or craft cue: a small signal, never a wash, measured 28 CIE76 from Ampache's #f8ac4c — the only warm competitor primary — and much deeper (L* 52 vs 70).
The ring is the sonar ping the brand is named for, not a container: it is open (60-degree gap at 3 o'clock) and carries the echo dot at its trailing end. No competitor on the shelf uses a ring mark.

Owner direction from the round-1 review: the light UI surface is deliberately a restrained warm off-white so the product keeps a light mode that belongs to the same environment as the warm dark ground. It is a UI surface, not a brand wash, and no competitor on the measured shelf uses a warm neutral.

rationale.claim: The light surface moved from pure white to a warm off-white (#F5F2EB) at owner direction, so the system reads as software with a warm dark mode rather than an all-dark product drifting toward retro hi-fi.
Echo Copper #B96A2E (L* 52.3) sits 28 CIE76 from Ampache's #f8ac4c and 35 from Plex's brand yellow — clear of the near-colour rule — and stays a small signal on both grounds.
Bricolage Grotesque carries display and text in one variable file (~126 KB); its I/l IoU 0.92 warning applies at small text sizes and is a known trade-off of the quirky cut.
The mark is kept to two primitives (open ring + dot) per owner direction: it must survive 16 px and become the interface's signal language rather than a decorated logo.

findings.message: light: link #9b541c on text #201b15 is 2.99:1, below 3.0:1 (links distinguishable from body text without underline (WCAG G183); WCAG 2, no rounding)
light: border #d6d1c6 on background #f5f2eb is 1.36:1, below 3.0:1 (borders: dividers are exempt, input outlines need 3:1; WCAG 2, no rounding)

suggested_fix.how: darken by OKLCH L -0.22, same hue

findings.message: dark: link #db8342 on text #f4f3f1 is 2.58:1, below 3.0:1 (underline links in dark mode (WCAG G183: without underline a link needs 3:1 against body text); WCAG 2, no rounding)
dark: border #454039 on background #17130e is 1.80:1, below 3.0:1 (borders: dividers are exempt, input outlines need 3:1; WCAG 2, no rounding)
Bricolage Grotesque lacks English auxiliary/punctuation characters: Ĕ Ĭ Ŏ ĕ ĭ ŏ ʻ
findings.suggested_fix: fine if the brand never writes them (loanwords, names); else another family

findings.message: Bricolage Grotesque: I/l look alike at small sizes (IoU 0.92 at 48 px)
findings.suggested_fix: no ss/cv alternates; choose another face for small text and data

findings.message: Bricolage Grotesque: ~126 KB WOFF2 for the brief's characters (one variable file, all weights; estimate)

findings.suggested_fix: give every primitive a semantic id so edits change one element per round

findings.message: accent resolves to #9b541c (UI tone); use brand-1 for #17130e
findings.suggested_fix: data-color="brand-1" (or logo.colors) for the exact brand colour

findings.message: sets too alike on the axes: A–B, A–C, B–C differ by 2+ steps on fewer than 2 axes (heuristic)
every set uses at least one AI-defaults item; build one set without any
